done_when: forge board --json and forge next --json leave out stories, tasks and fixes that were merged or done more than 7 days ago (they still show in the text board's history), with no cache; their output is otherwise unchanged; a command test on a repo with old finished items shows they are left out and that the number of git commands per call does not grow with them (no wall-clock timing); tests/test_machine_views.py stays within its time limit on Windows CI; new and earlier-adopted client repos get it, with a command test for each

The supplied close run passes six new retention/CRLF cases locally; the broader machine-view results are also local. findings.title: Not done: tests/test_machine_views.py stays within its time limit on Windows CI

findings.body: The previous advisory remains open. With a signed landed commit and log.showSignature=true, this git show includes signature-verification output, as specified by the [Git configuration contract](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-logshowSignature). src/forge/repo.py:144 returns the entire trimmed stdout; board.py:576 then inserts it into diff-tree input as a tree ID. That corrupts the snapshot batch used by both JSON commands and the human board. Resolve the tree with rev-parse <ref>^{tree}, or explicitly disable signature output.
findings.title: Disable signature output when reading the landed tree ID

findings.body: The previous advisory remains open. This comprehension expires historical additions even when their files no longer exist in landed_states. After reverting an old merge and removing its refs, a task or fix can restart with the same identity: src/forge/task.py:219–221 checks current file existence, and task.py:189,273 use that check when starting work. The new ongoing item is consequently omitted from both JSON views, and nextstep.py:209 also suppresses restarted-fix guidance. Require the path to exist in landed_states before expiring it from a historical merge date.
findings.title: Do not expire restarted tasks and fixes using reverted merge dates

why: forge board --json takes about 45 seconds and forge next --json about 10, so the pane's 10-second refresh would keep a core busy in every open Claude Code session
